output.reason: Reported recurrent seasonal sneezing, itchy eyes and nasal stuffiness in a 27-year-old asking for an OTC option can be managed with over-the-counter guidance now, with no reported feature requiring clinician assessment, prescribing or examination.
output.patientMessage: You can manage this yourself today: an OTC non-sedating antihistamine (cetirizine or loratadine), an OTC steroid nasal spray such as fluticasone (full effect takes 1–2 weeks), plus saline nasal rinses; limit oxymetazoline-type decongestant sprays to 3 days to avoid rebound stuffiness. If breathing difficulty or face/throat swelling develops, call 911. If symptoms turn one-sided, or fail to improve in 2 weeks, message a Counsel clinician.
differential: Seasonal allergic rhinitis with allergic conjunctivitis
Non-allergic or vasomotor rhinitis presenting similarly

redFlags.concern: Unilateral nasal obstruction or bloody discharge

citations.claim: Second-generation oral antihistamines such as cetirizine or loratadine are described as non-sedating and preferred for ongoing daily allergy symptom use.
citations.limitation: ED reference synthesis; doses listed are clinical knowledge, not individualized approval for this patient.
